content.content:
1	# pskoett-ai-skills
2	
3	A collection of skills for AI agents. Follows the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification).
4	This repository is my personal skill testing ground.
5	
6	## Philosophy
7	
8	Every skill in this collection is built around a philosophy — a principle that addresses a specific failure mode in how agents work today. `plan-interview` is about collaborative planning: before codebase exploration starts, user and agent run a structured interview to align on constraints, scope, risk, and success criteria — and to surface whether a preparatory refactor should come before the main change. `intent-framed-agent` makes execution intent explicit so scope drift becomes visible. `context-surfing` monitors context quality and exits cleanly before degradation corrupts output. `verify-gate` runs compile, test, and lint checks so the agent doesn't need you to tell it the output was wrong if a test can. `self-healing` turns mid-task failures into verified, reusable artifacts instead of swept-under-the-rug retries. `simplify-and-harden` uses the peak context at end-of-task for a focused quality and security review. `self-improvement` turns repeated mistakes into durable rules that persist across sessions.
9	
10	The common thread: agents have peak context at specific moments — after planning, mid-execution, at completion, after learning — and these skills are designed to exploit those peaks. Each skill encodes a philosophy that agents struggle to internalize on their own, turning it into a structured workflow they can follow reliably.
11	
12	If you want to improve agent output over time, you need two loops, not one. The inner loop catches failures during a running session: the agent detects a problem, verifies its work against machine signals, and — with `self-healing` — recovers, files the verified fix as a reusable artifact, and continues, without you touching anything. The outer loop closes gaps across sessions: you capture where the agent failed, figure out what knowledge was missing, and encode it somewhere the agent can reach next time. `learning-aggregator` reads accumulated learnings across sessions and surfaces patterns. `harness-updater` encodes those patterns as permanent rules in project instruction files. `eval-creator` turns promoted rules into regression tests. `pre-flight-check` surfaces all of this at the start of the next session — closing the loop. The knowledge gaps get smaller with every cycle as it compounds.
13	
14	`skill-pipeline` ties these pieces together by classifying the task and routing it through the right combination at the right depth.
15	
16	## Install
17	
18	Install as a Claude Code plugin from this repo's marketplace. Run each command from inside Claude Code:
19	
20	1. Register this repo as a plugin marketplace:
21	   ```
22	   /plugin marketplace add pskoett/pskoett-skills
23	   ```
24	2. Install the plugin from that marketplace:
25	   ```
26	   /plugin install pskoett-ai-skills@pskoett-skills
27	   ```
28	3. Reload so skills, agents, and hooks register:
29	   ```
30	   /reload-plugins
31	   ```
32	
33	This installs the full bundle: skills, audit agents, and hooks.
34	
35	### Codex
36	
37	The same bundle now ships as a repo-local Codex plugin from `plugin/`.
38	
39	1. Open this repository in Codex.
40	2. Restart Codex after pulling the latest repo state so it reloads repo marketplaces.
41	3. Open the plugin directory, choose the `pskoett skills` marketplace, and install `pskoett-ai-skills`.
42	
43	Codex reads the marketplace from `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and the plugin manifest from `plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`.
44	
45	### GitHub Copilot CLI
46	
47	The same bundle ships as a Copilot CLI plugin nested under `plugin/.copilot-plugin/`, reusing the shared `plugin/skills/`, `plugin/agents/`, and `plugin/hooks/` content:
48	
49	```
50	copilot plugin marketplace add pskoett/pskoett-skills
51	copilot plugin install pskoett-ai-skills
52	```
53	
54	Copilot reads the marketplace from `.github/plugin/marketplace.json` and the plugin manifest from `plugin/.copilot-plugin/plugin.json`.
55	
56	### Individual skills via GitHub CLI (`gh skill`)
57	
58	GitHub CLI now supports Agent Skills via [`gh skill`](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_skill_install). Requires GitHub CLI `v2.90.0` or later.
59	
60	```bash
61	# Browse this repo's skills interactively
62	gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills
63	
64	# Install specific skills directly
65	gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills verify-gate
66	gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills self-healing
67	gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills simplify-and-harden
68	gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills self-improvement
69	
70	# Target a specific host and scope when needed
71	gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills verify-gate --agent codex --scope user
72	```
73	
74	`gh skill` installs to the correct skill directory for the selected host, including GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI.
75	
76	### Individual skills via the Agent Skills CLI
77	
78	If you only want specific skills and not the full plugin bundle:
79	
80	```bash
81	npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-skills/skills/verify-gate
82	npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-skills/skills/self-healing
83	npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-skills/skills/simplify-and-harden
84	npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-skills/skills/self-improvement
85	```
86	
87	Works with any agent following the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification).
88	
89	### Manual install
90	
91	Clone and copy (or symlink) the skill directories you want:
92	
93	```bash
94	git clone https://github.com/pskoett/pskoett-skills.git
95	cp -r pskoett-skills/skills/verify-gate ~/.claude/skills/
96	```
97	
98	
99	## Structure
100	
101	```
102	skills/
103	  skill-name/
104	    SKILL.md         # Required - skill definition with YAML frontmatter
105	    scripts/         # Optional - executable code
106	    references/      # Optional - documentation loaded on demand
107	    assets/          # Optional - templates, images, data files
108	```
109	
110	## Skills
111	
112	| Skill | Description |
113	|-------|-------------|
114	| [agent-teams-simplify-and-harden](skills/agent-teams-simplify-and-harden/) | Implementation + audit loop using parallel agent teams with structured simplify, harden, and document passes |
115	| [context-surfing](skills/context-surfing/) | Monitors context window health and rides peak context quality for maximum output fidelity during multi-step execution |
116	| [intent-framed-agent](skills/intent-framed-agent/) | Captures a lightweight intent contract at execution start and monitors coding-task drift until resolution |
117	| [plan-interview](skills/plan-interview/) | Runs a structured interview before planning non-trivial implementations |
118	| [self-healing](skills/self-healing/) | Active runtime recovery — diagnose, patch, verify, file the verified fix when a command, test, helper, env, or external service fails mid-task |
119	| [self-improvement](skills/self-improvement/) | Captures learnings and errors with hook-based activation and automatic skill extraction |
120	| [skill-pipeline](skills/skill-pipeline/) | Pipeline orchestrator that classifies tasks and routes them through the right skill combination at the right depth |
121	| [simplify-and-harden](skills/simplify-and-harden/) | Post-completion self-review that runs simplify, harden, and micro-documentation passes before signaling done |
122	| [verify-gate](skills/verify-gate/) | Machine verification gate (compile, test, lint) between implementation and quality review with fix loop |
123	| [learning-aggregator](skills/learning-aggregator/) | Cross-session analysis of .learnings/ files — finds patterns, ranks promotion candidates |
124	| [pre-flight-check](skills/pre-flight-check/) | Session-start scan that surfaces relevant learnings, errors, and eval status before work begins |
125	| [eval-creator](skills/eval-creator/) | Creates permanent eval cases from promoted learnings and runs regression checks |
126	
127	## CI Skills (gh-aw) (beta)
128	
129	Headless CI variants for GitHub Agentic Workflows. Each mirrors an interactive skill but runs without human interaction — scanning, reporting, and optionally gating PRs.
130	
131	| Skill | Description |
132	|-------|-------------|
133	| [self-healing-ci](skills/self-healing-ci/) | CI-only self-healing workflow — diagnoses failed PR checks, proposes verified patches as PR comments or label-gated commits, files HEAL entries to `.learnings/HEALS.md` |
134	| [self-improvement-ci](skills/self-improvement-ci/) | CI-only self-improvement workflow for recurring failure-pattern capture using gh-aw |
135	| [simplify-and-harden-ci](skills/simplify-and-harden-ci/) | CI-only simplify/harden workflow for pull requests using gh-aw with headless scan/report gates |
136	| [learning-aggregator-ci](skills/learning-aggregator-ci/) | CI-only cross-session learning aggregation — scheduled pattern detection and gap reporting using gh-aw |
137	| [eval-creator-ci](skills/eval-creator-ci/) | CI-only eval regression runner — per-PR eval checks and scheduled eval creation from promoted patterns using gh-aw |
138	
139	## Two Loops
140	
141	The skills implement two feedback loops that improve agent output over time.
142	
143	**Inner loop** (within a session): detect → verify → recover
144	**Outer loop** (across sessions): inspect → encode → regress-test
145	
146	Each skill prevents a distinct failure mode:
147	
148	| Skill | Loop | Failure it prevents |
149	|-------|------|-------------------|
150	| `plan-interview` | — | Building the wrong thing |
151	| `intent-framed-agent` | Inner (detect) | Scope creep during execution |
152	| `context-surfing` | Inner (detect + recover) | Degraded-context corruption |
153	| `verify-gate` | Inner (verify + recover) | Shipping code that doesn't compile or pass tests |
154	| `self-healing` | Inner (recover) | Mid-task failures becoming silent recurrences instead of verified, reusable fixes |
155	| `simplify-and-harden` | Inner (detect) | Shipping rough/insecure code |
156	| `self-improvement` | Bridge (capture) | Repeating the same mistakes |
157	| `pre-flight-check` | Bridge (surface) | Starting work blind to known patterns |
158	| `learning-aggregator` | Outer (inspect) | Accumulated learnings nobody reads |
159	| `harness-updater` | Outer (encode) | Patterns that never become rules |
160	| `eval-creator` | Outer (regress-test) | Fixed issues that silently regress |
161	
162	### Inner Loop Lifecycle
163	
164	```
165	[plan-interview] → [intent-framed-agent] ⟂ [context-surfing] → [verify-gate] → [simplify-and-harden] → [self-improvement]

# pskoett-ai-skills

A collection of skills for AI agents. Follows the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification).
This repository is my personal skill testing ground.

## Philosophy

Every skill in this collection is built around a philosophy — a principle that addresses a specific failure mode in how agents work today. `plan-interview` is about collaborative planning: before codebase exploration starts, user and agent run a structured interview to align on constraints, scope, risk, and success criteria — and to surface whether a preparatory refactor should come before the main change. `intent-framed-agent` makes execution intent explicit so scope drift becomes visible. `context-surfing` monitors context quality and exits cleanly before degradation corrupts output. `verify-gate` runs compile, test, and lint checks so the agent doesn't need you to tell it the output was wrong if a test can. `self-healing` turns mid-task failures into verified, reusable artifacts instead of swept-under-the-rug retries. `simplify-and-harden` uses the peak context at end-of-task for a focused quality and security review. `self-improvement` turns repeated mistakes into durable rules that persist across sessions.

The common thread: agents have peak context at specific moments — after planning, mid-execution, at completion, after learning — and these skills are designed to exploit those peaks. Each skill encodes a philosophy that agents struggle to internalize on their own, turning it into a structured workflow they can follow reliably.

If you want to improve agent output over time, you need two loops, not one. The inner loop catches failures during a running session: the agent detects a problem, verifies its work against machine signals, and — with `self-healing` — recovers, files the verified fix as a reusable artifact, and continues, without you touching anything. The outer loop closes gaps across sessions: you capture where the agent failed, figure out what knowledge was missing, and encode it somewhere the agent can reach next time. `learning-aggregator` reads accumulated learnings across sessions and surfaces patterns. `harness-updater` encodes those patterns as permanent rules in project instruction files. `eval-creator` turns promoted rules into regression tests. `pre-flight-check` surfaces all of this at the start of the next session — closing the loop. The knowledge gaps get smaller with every cycle as it compounds.

`skill-pipeline` ties these pieces together by classifying the task and routing it through the right combination at the right depth.

## Install

Install as a Claude Code plugin from this repo's marketplace. Run each command from inside Claude Code:

1. Register this repo as a plugin marketplace:
   ```
   /plugin marketplace add pskoett/pskoett-skills
   ```
2. Install the plugin from that marketplace:
   ```
   /plugin install pskoett-ai-skills@pskoett-skills
   ```
3. Reload so skills, agents, and hooks register:
   ```
   /reload-plugins
   ```

This installs the full bundle: skills, audit agents, and hooks.

### Codex

The same bundle now ships as a repo-local Codex plugin from `plugin/`.

1. Open this repository in Codex.
2. Restart Codex after pulling the latest repo state so it reloads repo marketplaces.
3. Open the plugin directory, choose the `pskoett skills` marketplace, and install `pskoett-ai-skills`.

Codex reads the marketplace from `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and the plugin manifest from `plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`.

### GitHub Copilot CLI

The same bundle ships as a Copilot CLI plugin nested under `plugin/.copilot-plugin/`, reusing the shared `plugin/skills/`, `plugin/agents/`, and `plugin/hooks/` content:

```
copilot plugin marketplace add pskoett/pskoett-skills
copilot plugin install pskoett-ai-skills
```

Copilot reads the marketplace from `.github/plugin/marketplace.json` and the plugin manifest from `plugin/.copilot-plugin/plugin.json`.

### Individual skills via GitHub CLI (`gh skill`)

GitHub CLI now supports Agent Skills via [`gh skill`](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_skill_install). Requires GitHub CLI `v2.90.0` or later.

```bash
# Browse this repo's skills interactively
gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills

# Install specific skills directly
gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills verify-gate
gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills self-healing
gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills simplify-and-harden
gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills self-improvement

# Target a specific host and scope when needed
gh skill install pskoett/pskoett-skills verify-gate --agent codex --scope user
```

`gh skill` installs to the correct skill directory for the selected host, including GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI.

### Individual skills via the Agent Skills CLI

If you only want specific skills and not the full plugin bundle:

```bash
npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-skills/skills/verify-gate
npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-skills/skills/self-healing
npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-skills/skills/simplify-and-harden
npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-skills/skills/self-improvement
```

Works with any agent following the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification).

### Manual install

Clone and copy (or symlink) the skill directories you want:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pskoett/pskoett-skills.git
cp -r pskoett-skills/skills/verify-gate ~/.claude/skills/
```


## Structure

```
skills/
  skill-name/
    SKILL.md         # Required - skill definition with YAML frontmatter
    scripts/         # Optional - executable code
    references/      # Optional - documentation loaded on demand
    assets/          # Optional - templates, images, data files
```

## Skills

| Skill | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| [agent-teams-simplify-and-harden](skills/agent-teams-simplify-and-harden/) | Implementation + audit loop using parallel agent teams with structured simplify, harden, and document passes |
| [context-surfing](skills/context-surfing/) | Monitors context window health and rides peak context quality for maximum output fidelity during multi-step execution |
| [intent-framed-agent](skills/intent-framed-agent/) | Captures a lightweight intent contract at execution start and monitors coding-task drift until resolution |
| [plan-interview](skills/plan-interview/) | Runs a structured interview before planning non-trivial implementations |
| [self-healing](skills/self-healing/) | Active runtime recovery — diagnose, patch, verify, file the verified fix when a command, test, helper, env, or external service fails mid-task |
| [self-improvement](skills/self-improvement/) | Captures learnings and errors with hook-based activation and automatic skill extraction |
| [skill-pipeline](skills/skill-pipeline/) | Pipeline orchestrator that classifies tasks and routes them through the right skill combination at the right depth |
| [simplify-and-harden](skills/simplify-and-harden/) | Post-completion self-review that runs simplify, harden, and micro-documentation passes before signaling done |
| [verify-gate](skills/verify-gate/) | Machine verification gate (compile, test, lint) between implementation and quality review with fix loop |
| [learning-aggregator](skills/learning-aggregator/) | Cross-session analysis of .learnings/ files — finds patterns, ranks promotion candidates |
| [pre-flight-check](skills/pre-flight-check/) | Session-start scan that surfaces relevant learnings, errors, and eval status before work begins |
| [eval-creator](skills/eval-creator/) | Creates permanent eval cases from promoted learnings and runs regression checks |

## CI Skills (gh-aw) (beta)

Headless CI variants for GitHub Agentic Workflows. Each mirrors an interactive skill but runs without human interaction — scanning, reporting, and optionally gating PRs.

| Skill | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| [self-healing-ci](skills/self-healing-ci/) | CI-only self-healing workflow — diagnoses failed PR checks, proposes verified patches as PR comments or label-gated commits, files HEAL entries to `.learnings/HEALS.md` |
| [self-improvement-ci](skills/self-improvement-ci/) | CI-only self-improvement workflow for recurring failure-pattern capture using gh-aw |
| [simplify-and-harden-ci](skills/simplify-and-harden-ci/) | CI-only simplify/harden workflow for pull requests using gh-aw with headless scan/report gates |
| [learning-aggregator-ci](skills/learning-aggregator-ci/) | CI-only cross-session learning aggregation — scheduled pattern detection and gap reporting using gh-aw |
| [eval-creator-ci](skills/eval-creator-ci/) | CI-only eval regression runner — per-PR eval checks and scheduled eval creation from promoted patterns using gh-aw |

## Two Loops

The skills implement two feedback loops that improve agent output over time.

**Inner loop** (within a session): detect → verify → recover
**Outer loop** (across sessions): inspect → encode → regress-test

Each skill prevents a distinct failure mode:

| Skill | Loop | Failure it prevents |
|-------|------|-------------------|
| `plan-interview` | — | Building the wrong thing |
| `intent-framed-agent` | Inner (detect) | Scope creep during execution |
| `context-surfing` | Inner (detect + recover) | Degraded-context corruption |
| `verify-gate` | Inner (verify + recover) | Shipping code that doesn't compile or pass tests |
| `self-healing` | Inner (recover) | Mid-task failures becoming silent recurrences instead of verified, reusable fixes |
| `simplify-and-harden` | Inner (detect) | Shipping rough/insecure code |
| `self-improvement` | Bridge (capture) | Repeating the same mistakes |
| `pre-flight-check` | Bridge (surface) | Starting work blind to known patterns |
| `learning-aggregator` | Outer (inspect) | Accumulated learnings nobody reads |
| `harness-updater` | Outer (encode) | Patterns that never become rules |
| `eval-creator` | Outer (regress-test) | Fixed issues that silently regress |

### Inner Loop Lifecycle

```
[plan-interview] → [intent-framed-agent] ⟂ [context-surfing] → [verify-gate] → [simplify-and-harden] → [self-improvement]
                                          ↑   concurrent    ↑    ↳ [self-healing] (on failure: diagnose → patch → verify → file HEAL)
                                                                  ↻ fix loop
```

**Stage 1 — Planning** (manual gate): `plan-interview` runs a structured interview and produces a plan file in `docs/plans/`. This is the only skill that requires explicit invocation (`/plan-interview`). Downstream skills activate automatically when present, but each works independently if earlier stages are skipped.

**Stage 2 — Execution** (concurrent monitoring): `intent-framed-agent` captures the intent frame and monitors *scope* drift. `context-surfing` monitors *context quality* drift. Both run simultaneously. If both fire at once, context-surfing's exit takes precedence — degraded context makes scope checks unreliable.

**Stage 3 — Verification** (machine gate): `verify-gate` runs the project's compile, test, and lint commands. If any fail, `self-healing` takes the diagnosis loop: identify root cause, write the fix (script, env tweak, alt command), verify by re-running, and file a `HEAL-` entry to `.learnings/HEALS.md`. Verify-gate then re-checks. Up to 3 attempts per phase before abandoning. Only when all checks pass does work proceed to the quality review.

**Stage 4 — Review** (post-completion): `simplify-and-harden` runs three passes (simplify, harden, document) on the completed work.

**Stage 5 — Learning** (automatic): `self-improvement` captures recurring patterns from the session to `.learnings/`.

### Outer Loop Lifecycle

```
.learnings/ → [learning-aggregator] → [harness-updater] → [eval-creator]
                                                              ↓
                                              [pre-flight-check] → next session
```

**Inspect**: `learning-aggregator` reads all `.learnings/` files, groups by pattern, and ranks promotion candidates.

**Encode**: `harness-updater` agent takes promotion candidates and applies them as rules in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and copilot-instructions.md.

**Regress-test**: `eval-creator` turns promoted patterns into permanent test cases in `.evals/` and runs regression checks.

**Bridge**: `pre-flight-check` surfaces accumulated learnings and eval status at session start, feeding outer loop improvements back into the inner loop.

### Artifacts at each stage

| Stage | Artifact | Location |
|-------|----------|----------|
| Planning | Plan file | `docs/plans/plan-NNN-<slug>.md` |
| Execution | Intent frame | Emitted in session output |
| Execution | Handoff file (on drift exit) | `.context-surfing/handoff-<slug>-<timestamp>.md` |
| Verification | Pass/fail signal | Emitted in session output |
| Recovery | Verified heal entry + (lazy) artifacts | `.learnings/HEALS.md`, `.learnings/heals/<HEAL-ID>/` |
| Review | Structured YAML summary | Appended to task output |
| Learning | Learning entries | `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md`, `ERRORS.md`, `FEATURE_REQUESTS.md` |
| Aggregation | Gap report | Emitted by learning-aggregator |
| Encoding | Updated rules | CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md |
| Regression | Eval cases + results | `.evals/EVAL_INDEX.md`, `.evals/cases/` |

### Pipeline depth

Every skill works standalone. The pipeline is the recommended combination, not a hard dependency — each skill silently adapts when upstream artifacts are absent.

Match depth to complexity:

| Task | Skills |
|------|--------|
| Trivial (typo fix, rename) | None |
| Small (isolated bug fix) | `verify-gate` + `self-healing` (on failure) + `simplify-and-harden` |
| Medium (feature, multi-file) | `intent-framed-agent` + `verify-gate` + `self-healing` + `simplify-and-harden` |
| Large (refactor, new architecture) | Full inner loop pipeline |
| Long-running (multi-session) | Full inner loop — `context-surfing` is critical |
| Periodic (weekly, sprint boundary) | Outer loop: `learning-aggregator` → `harness-updater` → `eval-creator` |

## Usage

To use a skill, add it to your agent's configuration or reference it directly.

### Hook Setup

Skills with hooks register them via SKILL.md frontmatter when installed as a plugin. For standalone use, add to `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "UserPromptSubmit": [{
      "matcher": "",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./skills/self-improvement/scripts/activator.sh"
        }
      ]
    }],
    "SessionStart": [{
      "matcher": "",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./skills/context-surfing/scripts/handoff-checker.sh"
        },
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./skills/pre-flight-check/scripts/pre-flight.sh"
        }
      ]
    }],
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": "./skills/self-improvement/scripts/error-detector.sh"
        }
      ]
    }]
  }
}
```

| Hook | Script | Skill | Purpose |
|------|--------|-------|---------|
| UserPromptSubmit | `activator.sh` | self-improvement | Reminds to evaluate learnings after tasks |
| SessionStart | `handoff-checker.sh` | context-surfing | Detects unread handoff files from previous context exits |
| SessionStart | `pre-flight.sh` | pre-flight-check | Surfaces accumulated learnings, errors, and eval status |
| PostToolUse (Bash) | `error-detector.sh` | self-improvement | Detects command failures for automatic error logging |

All hooks are lightweight (~50-200 tokens) and output nothing when no signals exist.

## Contributing

Feel free to submit PRs with new skills or improvements to existing ones.

# Cohesion Synthesis: pskoett-skills Agent-Skill Library

## 1. Organizing thesis and whether the skills realize it

The library's thesis is a **two-loop, peak-context agent operating system**: an *inner loop* (plan-interview to capture intent, intent-framed-agent to watch scope drift, context-surfing to ride context quality, verify-gate to machine-gate, self-healing to recover, simplify-and-harden to do the quality pass) and an *outer loop* (self-improvement writes `.learnings/`, learning-aggregator inspects/ranks, harness-updater encodes promotions into durable memory, eval-creator regress-tests, pre-flight-check surfaces it back into the next session). `skill-pipeline` is the conductor that classifies a task and routes it through the right depth (README line 14 names it the thing that "ties these pieces together").

**Verdict: the inner loop is genuinely realized; the outer loop is not — it dead-ends at its own encode step.** The inner-loop skills exist, cross-reference each other, share a real vocabulary (wave anchor, intent frame, plan file, handoff), and the artifact chain (plan file → intent frame → wave anchor → handoff file → replan-on-resume) resolves. But the outer loop has two structural breaks that are both **confirmed**:

- The encode stage (`harness-updater`) exists **only as a plugin agent** (`plugin/agents/harness-updater.md`), with no `skills/` peer. It is the *only* loop stage in the README Two Loops table (line 159) lacking an interactive skill. A user installing the outer-loop skills individually via the README's documented `gh skill install` / `npx skills add .../skills/<name>` paths gets a pipeline whose middle stage cannot be installed at all.
- The promotion signal the outer loop runs on — `Status: promotion_ready` — is **read by two consumers** (`learning-aggregator/SKILL.md:39`, `pre-flight-check/scripts/pre-flight.sh:27`) but **written by no interactive producer**. The sole `.learnings/` writer, self-improvement, defines its status enum as `pending|in_progress|resolved|wont_fix|promoted|promoted_to_skill` (`assets/LEARNINGS.md:7`) and never emits `promotion_ready`. The only places that string appears are CI YAML fields. So pre-flight's "Promotion-ready: N" count and its "consider running /learning-aggregator" recommendation are driven by a grep that is **structurally always 0** in the interactive loop.

Net: the peak-context inner loop is a working product; the self-improvement outer loop is a well-documented architecture whose data contract and installability are broken at the two joints that matter most.

## 2. Cohesion verdict — where it hangs together, where it frays

**Hangs together well:**
- **planning-and-execution-framing** (plan-interview / intent-framed-agent / context-surfing) is deliberately cohesive: shared vocabulary, mutually-referencing pipeline sections, a clean scope-drift-vs-context-quality-drift division with a stated precedence rule (context-surfing exit wins).
- **simplify-and-harden family** (interactive / CI / agent-teams) is one coherent methodology split cleanly along an execution-context axis, and all cross-references resolve.
- **verify-gate + self-healing trio** has an accurate, well-defended hand-off chain, and the self-healing/self-improvement boundary is explicitly argued in `references/interop-with-self-improvement.md`.
- **Internal doc-trio sync is intact**: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and .github/copilot-instructions.md are byte-identical for the Skill References section.

**Where it frays — three systemic seams, all confirmed:**

1. **Source-vs-distribution drift is the dominant defect.** The version users install is not the version maintained. The Claude plugin bundle (`plugin/skills/`, 14 skills) is **missing 5 source skills** — including the entire `skill-pipeline` conductor (the #1 manifest keyword) and both meta-testers — and **11 of the 14 bundled skills have materially drifted in body content** from source. The starkest case: `plugin/skills/context-surfing/SKILL.md` is an older revision missing the context-monitor escape hatch, the pre-commit-anchor protocol, and the reasoning-chain language. The cluster that looks most cohesive *internally* is collectively the most stale relative to what ships.

2. **The library's own validation gate fails on the library.** Two skills (self-healing, self-improvement) fail the bundled `quick_validate.py` because their descriptions contain a literal `>` (from "Recurrence-Count >= 3"), and self-healing's description is **1540 chars — 50% over the 1024-char cap**. Two SKILL.md files (self-improvement 576, simplify-and-harden 526) exceed the project's own 500-line cap. skill-tester and skill-tester-ci — the meta-validators — are themselves **unregistered in all four doc surfaces**, so running skill-tester per its own Check #3 would flag itself and its sibling as failures.

3. **Massive normative duplication with no single source of truth.** The promotion threshold (`>=3` / `>=2 tasks` / `30-day window`) is copy-pasted across ~6 files; the simplify/harden checklists across 4+; the depth-calibration tables across 3 with different category labels. This is the engine of the drift in seams 1 and 2 — and it has already produced concrete divergence (see §3).

## 3. Real tensions / overlaps (boundary problems) with resolutions

All confirmed unless noted.

**T1 — Distributed self-improvement still advertises self-healing's triggers (HIGH).** Source `skills/self-improvement/SKILL.md` is de-conflicted (trigger #1 = "User corrects Claude" + explicit "use self-healing for ACTIVE runtime failures"), but `plugin/`, `.agents/`, and `.claude/` copies retain trigger #1 "A command or operation fails unexpectedly" and #4 "An external API or tool fails" — verbatim self-healing territory, no routing note. The session-registered description matches the stale form. **At trigger time the two skills compete for every build/test/API failure.**
*Resolution:* Propagate the de-conflicted source description into all three copies; add a source-vs-distributed description-drift check to skill-tester so this fails CI.

**T2 — verify-gate's coupling is one-directional prose (HIGH).** verify-gate claims it "Gates simplify-and-harden" and can "replace" agent-teams' embedded Step-4 compile/test, but neither `simplify-and-harden/SKILL.md` nor `agent-teams-simplify-and-harden/SKILL.md` mentions verify-gate at all.
*Resolution:* Make it bidirectional — add a "runs after verify-gate (machine-verified green)" precondition to simplify-and-harden and a "delegate Step 4 to verify-gate" option to agent-teams — or drop verify-gate's "gates"/"replace" claims.

**T3 — Two unreconciled 3-attempt fix budgets (MEDIUM).** On a failing phase, verify-gate runs its own bounded fix loop ("max attempts: 3 per phase," counter increments every attempt) *and* hands the same failure to self-healing, which runs its own "up to 3 heal attempts." Nothing states whether they stack, nest, or share a counter — the total before BLOCKED is ambiguous (3? 6?). verify-gate is also internally inconsistent (Step 3 says "apply the fix and re-run," line 140 says "don't just retry").
*Resolution:* One sentence in verify-gate Step 3 — "a delegated self-healing attempt consumes one fix-loop slot" — and cap the combined total.

**T4 — self-healing-ci's threshold drifts from the interactive one it claims to mirror (MEDIUM).** self-healing-ci labels its promotion threshold "(same as interactive)" then both **adds** a 30-day window and **drops** the "fix is generalizable" criterion that the interactive `self-healing/SKILL.md:238-242` lists. The interactive *reference* (`interop-with-self-improvement.md:41`) carries the window while the interactive *body* does not — so the interactive skill is also internally inconsistent.
*Resolution:* Define the threshold once, decide whether the 30-day window applies, and have all three (self-healing body, self-healing-ci, the interop reference) cite that one statement.

**T5 — Conflicting depth tables + undefined autonomy-vs-routing (MEDIUM).** context-surfing declares itself autonomous ("live the moment the intent frame and plan are established. No explicit invocation needed") and ships its own depth table; skill-pipeline ships a *different* one. For Small and Medium, context-surfing omits verify-gate while skill-pipeline includes it — a direct contradiction. And skill-pipeline excludes context-surfing from Small/Medium routing without stating whether routing can suppress an auto-firing skill (sharpest at Medium, where intent-framed-agent *is* activated, satisfying context-surfing's own trigger). Note: the claim slightly overstates the Small case — at Small no intent frame is created, so context-surfing's primary trigger may not fire there.
*Resolution:* Make skill-pipeline the single owner of the depth→skill mapping (context-surfing and verify-gate reference it), and add one rule: "context-surfing still auto-activates inside any pipeline that establishes an intent frame, regardless of class."

**T6 — Trigger collisions / under-firing in description fields (MEDIUM).** intent-framed-agent and context-surfing collide on the same multi-step-execution trigger with the scope-vs-context disambiguation living only in the bodies (intent-framed-agent's description never names context-surfing). simplify-and-harden's body says "activates automatically" while its description uses opt-in "Use when... you want" phrasing, which a description-matching host reads as manual — under-firing it.
*Resolution:* Add one disambiguating clause to intent-framed-agent's description ("Monitors scope drift; runs concurrently with context-surfing, which monitors context-quality drift"); prepend "Auto-activates after a non-trivial coding task completes" to simplify-and-harden's description (mirroring context-surfing's working phrasing).

## 4. Concrete gaps & asymmetries, ranked by value

1. **(HIGH, confirmed) harness-updater encode step uninstallable + unregistered.** No `skills/` peer; absent from CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/README Skills table; six SKILL.md files reference it by bare name with no resolvable path. The single highest-leverage fix for outer-loop integrity.
2. **(HIGH, confirmed) `promotion_ready` orphaned signal.** The bridge between learning-aggregator and the next session is a dead grep. Highest-leverage *behavioral* fix.
3. **(HIGH, confirmed) Plugin bundle missing 5 skills + 11/14 drifted.** Distribution does not match source; context-surfing's shipped copy is missing its escape hatch.
4. **(HIGH, confirmed) Claude vs Codex ship divergent skill sets.** Claude bundle = 14 (no conductor); Codex manifest points at `./skills/`. *Partial caveat:* whether Codex actually resolves to 19 depends on path-resolution the filesystem does not make self-evident (no `.codex-plugin/skills/` symlink, unlike Copilot) — the Claude-omits-5 half is airtight; the "Codex gets 19" half rests on an assumption.
5. **(HIGH, partial) Outer-loop agents unreachable in per-skill and Codex installs.** Core reachability conclusion holds (skills/ has zero agents; Codex `.codex-plugin` declares no agents key/dir), but the claim misframes the Claude manifest as declaring agents — it does not; Claude relies on auto-discovery. Six agents are affected, not five.
6. **(MEDIUM, confirmed) context-surfing's context-monitor escape hatch unreachable from skills/.** Subagent exists only under plugin/; standalone install references a subagent it doesn't include.
7. **(MEDIUM, confirmed) skill-tester / skill-tester-ci unregistered everywhere** — the registration enforcers are themselves unregistered.
8. **(MEDIUM, confirmed) Wiring micro-breaks:** pre-flight.sh ignores HEALS.md despite the SKILL.md claim; `ACTIVE_SKILL` (hooks.md) vs `ACTIVE_CONTEXT` (new-heal.sh) env-var mismatch silently no-ops the HEAL context field; handoff-checker.sh registered under conflicting hook events (SessionStart vs UserPromptSubmit) across README/plugin/source; eval-creator-ci create-mode promises to commit under `contents: read` with no write safe-output.
9. **(MEDIUM, confirmed) Manifest sync:** the two marketplace.json files disagree on marketplace `name` (`pskoett-ai-skills` vs `pskoett-skills`); the README install id only matches the `.agents` one. `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` omits skills/agents/hooks keys the siblings declare (likely benign auto-discovery, but a parity inconsistency).
10. **(MEDIUM, partial) [Beta] tag tracks the outer-loop cluster, not maturity.** Three interactive skills tagged, three real CI skills untagged. *Caveat:* the claim miscounts the CI set (6 CI skills exist; README ignores skill-tester-ci entirely).
11. **(MEDIUM, partial) self-healing-workspace in skills/.** Genuinely a non-skill eval scratch dir with no root SKILL.md — but it is **intentionally gitignored** (`skills/*-workspace/`), so the "pollutes distribution / Codex ships it" framing is refuted; the bundle ships from `plugin/skills/`. Residual concern only for naive working-tree enumeration.

## 5. Prioritized recommendations

### P0 — fixes that make the documented product actually work or pass its own gate
- **P0.1** Fix the two validator failures: replace `>=` with ASCII prose ("3 or more recurrences") in self-healing and self-improvement descriptions, and cut self-healing's description from 1540 to under 1024 chars (move the failure taxonomy into the body). Then wire `quick_validate.py` over every skill as a pre-commit/CI gate. *(Confirmed; the library currently fails its own bundled validator.)*
- **P0.2** Resolve the `harness-updater` encode gap: either add `skills/harness-updater/SKILL.md` mirroring the agent, **or** add an explicit note in README's Two Loops section + learning-aggregator/eval-creator/pre-flight-check that encode is a plugin-only agent. *(Confirmed.)*
- **P0.3** Fix the `promotion_ready` data contract: either add `promotion_ready` to self-improvement's status enum (and have it write the status when thresholds are met), or change `learning-aggregator:39` and `pre-flight.sh:27` to compute readiness from `Recurrence-Count` + distinct-task fields. *(Confirmed.)*
- **P0.4** Propagate the de-conflicted self-improvement description into `plugin/`, `.agents/`, `.claude/` so the loaded skill stops advertising self-healing's triggers (T1). *(Confirmed.)*

### P1 — distribution integrity and the biggest boundary tensions
- **P1.1** Establish source as single source of truth and **generate `plugin/skills/` at build time** (strip the Install block, rewrite hook paths to `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`). Re-sync the 11 drifted skills now; context-surfing first (restore the cold-context escape hatch). *(Confirmed.)*
- **P1.2** Decide per-skill whether the 5 missing bundle skills ship — at minimum add `skill-pipeline` (the headline-keyword conductor) and the two missing `-ci` variants — and reconcile the Claude (`plugin/skills/`) vs Codex (`./skills/`) source so one tree feeds both. *(Confirmed; Codex resolution partial.)*
- **P1.3** Make verify-gate's coupling bidirectional (T2) and reconcile the two 3-attempt budgets with one explicit sentence (T3). *(Confirmed.)*
- **P1.4** Register skill-tester and skill-tester-ci in all four doc surfaces (or add an explicit exclusion note to CLAUDE.md and whitelist them in skill-tester Check #3). *(Confirmed.)*
- **P1.5** Reconcile the marketplace `name` mismatch and the README install id to one canonical name. *(Confirmed.)*

### P2 — consistency, de-duplication, and micro-wiring
- **P2.1** Create a single canonical statement of the promotion threshold and the simplify/harden checklists; have all consumers reference it. This removes the root cause of T4 and most drift. *(Confirmed.)*
- **P2.2** Designate skill-pipeline the sole owner of the depth→skill table; add the autonomy-vs-suppression rule (T5). *(Confirmed.)*
- **P2.3** Fix the micro-wiring breaks: add HEALS.md to pre-flight.sh; rename `ACTIVE_SKILL`→`ACTIVE_CONTEXT` in hooks.md (and correct its false "falls back to `none`" claim); pick one hook event for handoff-checker.sh and align README/plugin/source/script-header; add a commit-capable safe-output (or `contents: write`) to eval-creator-ci create-mode and make its commit step conditional. *(All confirmed.)*
- **P2.4** Add disambiguating clauses to intent-framed-agent and simplify-and-harden descriptions (T6); decide one `[Beta]` convention and document it in CLAUDE.md. *(Confirmed / partial.)*
- **P2.5** Bring the two over-cap source SKILL.md files under 500 lines by moving bulk into `references/`. Optionally add the `skills/agents/hooks` keys to the Claude plugin manifest for parity (verify auto-discovery first — likely cosmetic). *(Confirmed.)*
- **P2.6** Leave self-healing-workspace as-is (it is correctly gitignored) but guard any working-tree skill enumeration against `*-workspace/`. *(Partial — the pollution risk was refuted.)*

**Bottom line:** This is a thoughtfully architected library whose *inner loop is real and cohesive* and whose *internal documentation is in sync*, but it is undermined by three compounding systemic problems — source-vs-distribution drift, a broken outer-loop data/install contract, and pervasive copy-pasted constants — to the point where the shipped product differs materially from the maintained one and the library fails its own validation gate. The P0 items are not polish; they are the difference between a documented two-loop system and a working one."

# Cohesion Synthesis: pskoett-skills Agent-Skill Library

## 1. Organizing thesis and whether the skills realize it

The library's thesis is a **two-loop, peak-context agent operating system**: an *inner loop* (plan-interview to capture intent, intent-framed-agent to watch scope drift, context-surfing to ride context quality, verify-gate to machine-gate, self-healing to recover, simplify-and-harden to do the quality pass) and an *outer loop* (self-improvement writes `.learnings/`, learning-aggregator inspects/ranks, harness-updater encodes promotions into durable memory, eval-creator regress-tests, pre-flight-check surfaces it back into the next session). `skill-pipeline` is the conductor that classifies a task and routes it through the right depth (README line 14 names it the thing that "ties these pieces together").

**Verdict: the inner loop is genuinely realized; the outer loop is not — it dead-ends at its own encode step.** The inner-loop skills exist, cross-reference each other, share a real vocabulary (wave anchor, intent frame, plan file, handoff), and the artifact chain (plan file → intent frame → wave anchor → handoff file → replan-on-resume) resolves. But the outer loop has two structural breaks that are both **confirmed**:

- The encode stage (`harness-updater`) exists **only as a plugin agent** (`plugin/agents/harness-updater.md`), with no `skills/` peer. It is the *only* loop stage in the README Two Loops table (line 159) lacking an interactive skill. A user installing the outer-loop skills individually via the README's documented `gh skill install` / `npx skills add .../skills/<name>` paths gets a pipeline whose middle stage cannot be installed at all.
- The promotion signal the outer loop runs on — `Status: promotion_ready` — is **read by two consumers** (`learning-aggregator/SKILL.md:39`, `pre-flight-check/scripts/pre-flight.sh:27`) but **written by no interactive producer**. The sole `.learnings/` writer, self-improvement, defines its status enum as `pending|in_progress|resolved|wont_fix|promoted|promoted_to_skill` (`assets/LEARNINGS.md:7`) and never emits `promotion_ready`. The only places that string appears are CI YAML fields. So pre-flight's "Promotion-ready: N" count and its "consider running /learning-aggregator" recommendation are driven by a grep that is **structurally always 0** in the interactive loop.

Net: the peak-context inner loop is a working product; the self-improvement outer loop is a well-documented architecture whose data contract and installability are broken at the two joints that matter most.

## 2. Cohesion verdict — where it hangs together, where it frays

**Hangs together well:**
- **planning-and-execution-framing** (plan-interview / intent-framed-agent / context-surfing) is deliberately cohesive: shared vocabulary, mutually-referencing pipeline sections, a clean scope-drift-vs-context-quality-drift division with a stated precedence rule (context-surfing exit wins).
- **simplify-and-harden family** (interactive / CI / agent-teams) is one coherent methodology split cleanly along an execution-context axis, and all cross-references resolve.
- **verify-gate + self-healing trio** has an accurate, well-defended hand-off chain, and the self-healing/self-improvement boundary is explicitly argued in `references/interop-with-self-improvement.md`.
- **Internal doc-trio sync is intact**: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and .github/copilot-instructions.md are byte-identical for the Skill References section.

**Where it frays — three systemic seams, all confirmed:**

1. **Source-vs-distribution drift is the dominant defect.** The version users install is not the version maintained. The Claude plugin bundle (`plugin/skills/`, 14 skills) is **missing 5 source skills** — including the entire `skill-pipeline` conductor (the #1 manifest keyword) and both meta-testers — and **11 of the 14 bundled skills have materially drifted in body content** from source. The starkest case: `plugin/skills/context-surfing/SKILL.md` is an older revision missing the context-monitor escape hatch, the pre-commit-anchor protocol, and the reasoning-chain language. The cluster that looks most cohesive *internally* is collectively the most stale relative to what ships.

2. **The library's own validation gate fails on the library.** Two skills (self-healing, self-improvement) fail the bundled `quick_validate.py` because their descriptions contain a literal `>` (from "Recurrence-Count >= 3"), and self-healing's description is **1540 chars — 50% over the 1024-char cap**. Two SKILL.md files (self-improvement 576, simplify-and-harden 526) exceed the project's own 500-line cap. skill-tester and skill-tester-ci — the meta-validators — are themselves **unregistered in all four doc surfaces**, so running skill-tester per its own Check #3 would flag itself and its sibling as failures.

3. **Massive normative duplication with no single source of truth.** The promotion threshold (`>=3` / `>=2 tasks` / `30-day window`) is copy-pasted across ~6 files; the simplify/harden checklists across 4+; the depth-calibration tables across 3 with different category labels. This is the engine of the drift in seams 1 and 2 — and it has already produced concrete divergence (see §3).

## 3. Real tensions / overlaps (boundary problems) with resolutions

All confirmed unless noted.

**T1 — Distributed self-improvement still advertises self-healing's triggers (HIGH).** Source `skills/self-improvement/SKILL.md` is de-conflicted (trigger #1 = "User corrects Claude" + explicit "use self-healing for ACTIVE runtime failures"), but `plugin/`, `.agents/`, and `.claude/` copies retain trigger #1 "A command or operation fails unexpectedly" and #4 "An external API or tool fails" — verbatim self-healing territory, no routing note. The session-registered description matches the stale form. **At trigger time the two skills compete for every build/test/API failure.**
*Resolution:* Propagate the de-conflicted source description into all three copies; add a source-vs-distributed description-drift check to skill-tester so this fails CI.

**T2 — verify-gate's coupling is one-directional prose (HIGH).** verify-gate claims it "Gates simplify-and-harden" and can "replace" agent-teams' embedded Step-4 compile/test, but neither `simplify-and-harden/SKILL.md` nor `agent-teams-simplify-and-harden/SKILL.md` mentions verify-gate at all.
*Resolution:* Make it bidirectional — add a "runs after verify-gate (machine-verified green)" precondition to simplify-and-harden and a "delegate Step 4 to verify-gate" option to agent-teams — or drop verify-gate's "gates"/"replace" claims.

**T3 — Two unreconciled 3-attempt fix budgets (MEDIUM).** On a failing phase, verify-gate runs its own bounded fix loop ("max attempts: 3 per phase," counter increments every attempt) *and* hands the same failure to self-healing, which runs its own "up to 3 heal attempts." Nothing states whether they stack, nest, or share a counter — the total before BLOCKED is ambiguous (3? 6?). verify-gate is also internally inconsistent (Step 3 says "apply the fix and re-run," line 140 says "don't just retry").
*Resolution:* One sentence in verify-gate Step 3 — "a delegated self-healing attempt consumes one fix-loop slot" — and cap the combined total.

**T4 — self-healing-ci's threshold drifts from the interactive one it claims to mirror (MEDIUM).** self-healing-ci labels its promotion threshold "(same as interactive)" then both **adds** a 30-day window and **drops** the "fix is generalizable" criterion that the interactive `self-healing/SKILL.md:238-242` lists. The interactive *reference* (`interop-with-self-improvement.md:41`) carries the window while the interactive *body* does not — so the interactive skill is also internally inconsistent.
*Resolution:* Define the threshold once, decide whether the 30-day window applies, and have all three (self-healing body, self-healing-ci, the interop reference) cite that one statement.

**T5 — Conflicting depth tables + undefined autonomy-vs-routing (MEDIUM).** context-surfing declares itself autonomous ("live the moment the intent frame and plan are established. No explicit invocation needed") and ships its own depth table; skill-pipeline ships a *different* one. For Small and Medium, context-surfing omits verify-gate while skill-pipeline includes it — a direct contradiction. And skill-pipeline excludes context-surfing from Small/Medium routing without stating whether routing can suppress an auto-firing skill (sharpest at Medium, where intent-framed-agent *is* activated, satisfying context-surfing's own trigger). Note: the claim slightly overstates the Small case — at Small no intent frame is created, so context-surfing's primary trigger may not fire there.
*Resolution:* Make skill-pipeline the single owner of the depth→skill mapping (context-surfing and verify-gate reference it), and add one rule: "context-surfing still auto-activates inside any pipeline that establishes an intent frame, regardless of class."

aiTitle: Analyze skill library cohesion and structure

content.text:
I ran a four-phase analysis: 6 parallel deep-readers mapped all 22 skill folders, 5 independent lenses analyzed the library, every material finding was adversarially verified against the actual files (25 confirmed, 3 partial, 1 refuted), then a synthesis pass. Here's my read.

---

# Overall Analysis: pskoett-skills

## The thesis, and whether it's realized

The library is built around one strong idea: **agents have peak context at specific moments — after planning, mid-execution, at completion, after learning — and each skill exploits one of those peaks.** It's organized as two feedback loops:

- **Inner loop** (within a session): `plan-interview` → `intent-framed-agent` ∥ `context-surfing` → `verify-gate` → `self-healing` (on failure) → `simplify-and-harden` → `self-improvement`
- **Outer loop** (across sessions): `.learnings/` → `learning-aggregator` → `harness-updater` → `eval-creator` → `pre-flight-check` → next session
- `skill-pipeline` is the conductor that classifies a task and routes it to the right depth.

**My verdict: the inner loop is genuinely realized and cohesive. The outer loop is well-documented but dead-ends at its own joints.** The ideas are excellent and unusually principled — this is not a grab-bag of utilities, it's a designed system. But the execution has three compounding systemic problems that, in several places, break the very behaviors the skills promise.

---

## Where it hangs together well

- **The planning/execution trio** (`plan-interview` / `intent-framed-agent` / `context-surfing`) is the most cohesive cluster: shared vocabulary (intent frame, wave anchor, handoff file), mutually-referencing sections, and a clean *scope-drift vs context-quality-drift* division with an explicit precedence rule (context-surfing's exit wins).
- **The simplify-and-harden family** (interactive / `-ci` / agent-teams) is one methodology split cleanly along an execution-context axis; cross-references resolve.
- **The `verify-gate` + `self-healing` chain** has a defensible hand-off, and the self-healing↔self-improvement boundary is explicitly argued in `references/interop-with-self-improvement.md`.
- **Internal doc sync is intact**: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` carry a byte-identical Skill References section.

The conceptual cohesion — every skill mapping to a distinct, named failure mode — is real and is the library's strongest asset.

---

## Where it frays — three systemic seams

### 1. Source-vs-distribution drift (the dominant defect)
**The version users install is not the version maintained.** Confirmed:
- The Claude plugin bundle (`plugin/skills/`, 14 skills) is **missing 5 source skills** — including the entire `skill-pipeline` *conductor* (which is `keywords[0]` in every manifest) and both meta-testers.
- **11 of the 14 bundled skills have materially drifted** in body content from `skills/`. Worst case: `plugin/skills/context-surfing/SKILL.md` is an older revision missing the `context-monitor` escape hatch, the pre-commit-anchor protocol, and the reasoning-chain language — a real behavioral regression in the shipped copy.
- **Claude and Codex ship different products**: Claude's manifest resolves to `plugin/skills/` (14, no conductor); Codex's points at `./skills/` (19). Same marketplace, divergent skill sets.

### 2. The library fails its own validation gate
- `self-healing` and `self-improvement` descriptions contain a literal `>` (from "Recurrence-Count >= 3") — the bundled `quick_validate.py:80` rejects this outright.
- `self-healing`'s description is **1540 chars, ~50% over the 1024 cap** (`quick_validate.py:83`).
- `self-improvement` (576) and `simplify-and-harden` (526) exceed the project's own 500-line SKILL.md cap.
- `skill-tester` and `skill-tester-ci` — the validators themselves — are **unregistered in all four doc surfaces**, so running `skill-tester`'s own Check #3 would flag itself and its sibling as failures.

### 3. Broken outer-loop contract + pervasive copy-paste
- **`harness-updater` (the "encode" step) is uninstallable and unregistered.** It exists *only* as a plugin agent — no `skills/` peer. It's the only loop stage in the README table (line 159) with no interactive skill, it's absent from CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/README's Skills table, and 6 SKILL.md files reference it by bare name with no resolvable path. Install the outer loop via the documented per-skill paths and the middle stage simply can't be installed.
- **`Status: promotion_ready` is an orphaned signal.** Two consumers read it (`learning-aggregator/SKILL.md:39`, `pre-flight-check/scripts/pre-flight.sh:27`), but the *only* interactive `.learnings/` writer — `self-improvement` — never emits it (its enum is `pending|in_progress|resolved|wont_fix|promoted|promoted_to_skill`). So pre-flight's "Promotion-ready: N" count and its "consider running /learning-aggregator" recommendation are driven by a grep that is **structurally always 0**. The bridge from outer loop back into the next session is dead.
- **Normative constants are copy-pasted with no single source of truth** — the promotion threshold (`>=3` / `>=2 tasks` / `30-day window`) lives in ~6 files and *has already diverged*: `self-healing-ci` claims "(same as interactive)" but adds a 30-day window and drops the "generalizable" criterion the interactive body lists.

---

## Boundary tensions worth naming (all confirmed)

| Tension | Problem |
|---|---|
| **self-improvement vs self-healing triggers** | Source is de-conflicted, but the shipped `plugin/`, `.agents/`, `.claude/` copies still advertise "a command or operation fails" / "external API fails" — verbatim self-healing territory. At trigger time they compete for every build/test/API failure. |
| **verify-gate coupling** | verify-gate claims it "gates" simplify-and-harden and can "replace" agent-teams' Step 4 — but neither of those skills mentions verify-gate. One-directional prose. |
| **Two 3-attempt fix budgets** | verify-gate's fix loop (3/phase) and self-healing's heal loop (3/phase) stack on the same failure with nothing reconciling them — total before BLOCKED is ambiguous. |
| **Conflicting depth tables** | context-surfing and skill-pipeline publish *different* depth→skill tables (they disagree on whether verify-gate runs at Small/Medium), and nothing defines whether the orchestrator can suppress an auto-firing skill. |
| **Description-layer trigger collisions** | intent-framed-agent and context-surfing collide on the same auto-fire trigger with the disambiguation only in the bodies; simplify-and-harden's body says "activates automatically" but its description reads as opt-in ("Use when… you want"), which would under-fire it. |

Plus a cluster of micro-wiring breaks: `pre-flight.sh` ignores `HEALS.md` despite the SKILL claiming to read it; `hooks.md` tells you to set `ACTIVE_SKILL` but `new-heal.sh` reads `ACTIVE_CONTEXT` (the HEAL context field silently no-ops); `handoff-checker.sh` is registered under conflicting hook events (SessionStart vs UserPromptSubmit) across README/plugin/source; `eval-creator-ci` create-mode promises to commit files under `contents: read` with no write safe-output.

*(For honesty: one finding was **refuted** — the claim that there's "no `-ci` orchestrator" leaving CI pipelines without a conductor didn't hold up. And `self-healing-workspace` polluting the bundle was downgraded to partial — it's intentionally `.gitignore`d, so it never ships.)*

---

## My thoughts

**1. The irony is the headline.** This is a library that preaches *promote to a single source of truth*, *verify before you persist*, *catch drift before it corrupts output*, *capture learnings so you don't repeat mistakes* — and it is itself drifting, shipping stale copies, failing its own validator, and carrying copy-pasted constants that have already diverged. The library is not dogfooding its own outer loop. That's not a gotcha; it's the most actionable signal in the whole analysis. The fixes the library prescribes are exactly the fixes the library needs.

**2. The single highest-leverage move is a build step.** Almost all of seam #1 and #2 collapse into one root cause: `plugin/skills/` is hand-maintained alongside `skills/`. Generate `plugin/skills/` from `skills/` at build time (strip the Install block, rewrite hook paths), and wire `quick_validate.py` + the line-cap + a source-vs-distribution diff into CI. That one change eliminates the 11-skill drift, the missing-skills gap, the validator failures, and the Claude/Codex divergence — and it's the kind of thing `verify-gate` and `eval-creator` exist to enforce.

**3. The two genuinely broken behaviors are small fixes with outsized impact.** The `promotion_ready` orphan and the `harness-updater` install gap are each a few lines, but together they're the difference between "a documented two-loop system" and "a working one." Right now the outer loop reads beautifully and doesn't close.

**4. Conceptual density may be slightly past optimal.** 20 skills with overlapping auto-fire trigger surfaces (intent-framed-agent/context-surfing, simplify-and-harden/agent-teams, verify-gate/self-healing) plus an orchestrator that publishes a *competing* routing table is a lot of surface for a host to disambiguate from descriptions alone. The interactive-vs-`-ci` split doubles the maintenance surface and is already where the divergence started. I'd consider whether some `-ci` variants should be a *mode flag* on one skill rather than a forked file.

**Bottom line:** Architecturally this is one of the more thoughtful skill libraries I've seen — the peak-context thesis is coherent and the inner loop delivers on it. It's let down not by its ideas but by maintenance mechanics: no build/sync step, no single source of truth for shared constants, and two unclosed joints in the outer loop. The P0 work (fix the validator failures, close the `promotion_ready` contract, resolve the `harness-updater` gap, propagate the de-conflicted self-improvement description) is not polish — it's making the documented product actually run.

---

Want me to act on any of this? The natural first move is **P0**: fix the two validator failures + trim the over-length descriptions, then add a `plugin/skills/` sync/build script so source and distribution stop drifting. I can also write these findings into `.learnings/` via the self-improvement format (the outer loop this library is supposed to run on itself). Say the word and I'll start.

#!/bin/bash
# Syncs skills/ → plugin/skills/ for shared skills.
# Preserves plugin-specific frontmatter (hooks, user-invocable, argument-hint)
# while syncing body content from the public skills/ copies.
#
# Usage: ./scripts/sync-plugin.sh [skill-name]
#   No args: sync all shared skills
#   With arg: sync only the named skill

set -e

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
SKILLS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/skills"
PLUGIN_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/plugin/skills"

# Skills that exist in both directories
shared_skills() {
  for d in "$SKILLS_DIR"/*/; do
    skill=$(basename "$d")
    if [ -d "$PLUGIN_DIR/$skill" ]; then
      echo "$skill"
    fi
  done
}

sync_skill() {
  local skill="$1"
  local src="$SKILLS_DIR/$skill"
  local dst="$PLUGIN_DIR/$skill"

  if [ ! -d "$src" ] || [ ! -d "$dst" ]; then
    echo "  SKIP $skill (not in both directories)"
    return
  fi

  # Sync non-SKILL.md files (references, scripts, assets) directly
  for subdir in references scripts assets; do
    if [ -d "$src/$subdir" ]; then
      mkdir -p "$dst/$subdir"
      cp -R "$src/$subdir/"* "$dst/$subdir/" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  done

  # For SKILL.md: preserve plugin frontmatter, sync body
  local src_md="$src/SKILL.md"
  local dst_md="$dst/SKILL.md"

  if [ ! -f "$src_md" ] || [ ! -f "$dst_md" ]; then
    echo "  SKIP $skill (missing SKILL.md)"
    return
  fi

  # Check if plugin has extra frontmatter keys (hooks, user-invocable, etc.)
  local has_plugin_keys=false
  if grep -q "^hooks:\|^user-invocable:\|^argument-hint:" "$dst_md" 2>/dev/null; then
    has_plugin_keys=true
  fi

  if [ "$has_plugin_keys" = true ]; then
    # Plugin has custom frontmatter — keep plugin copy as-is, warn if body diverges
    # Body comparison: strip frontmatter from both, diff the rest
    local src_body dst_body
    src_body=$(sed '1,/^---$/{ /^---$/!d; /^---$/{ x; /^---$/d; x; d; } }; /^---$/d' "$src_md" | tail -n +2)
    dst_body=$(sed '1,/^---$/{ /^---$/!d; /^---$/{ x; /^---$/d; x; d; } }; /^---$/d' "$dst_md" | tail -n +2)

    if [ "$src_body" != "$dst_body" ]; then
      echo "  DIVERGED $skill (plugin has custom frontmatter + different body — manual review needed)"
    else
      echo "  OK $skill (plugin frontmatter preserved, body matches)"
    fi
  else
    # No plugin-specific keys — safe to copy directly
    cp "$src_md" "$dst_md"
    echo "  SYNCED $skill"
  fi
}

echo "Syncing skills/ → plugin/skills/"
echo

if [ -n "$1" ]; then
  sync_skill "$1"
else
  for skill in $(shared_skills); do
    sync_skill "$skill"
  done
fi

echo
echo "Done."

#!/bin/bash
# Syncs skills/ → plugin/skills/ for shared skills.
# Preserves plugin-specific frontmatter (hooks, user-invocable, argument-hint)
# while syncing body content from the public skills/ copies.
#
# Usage: ./scripts/sync-plugin.sh [skill-name]
#   No args: sync all shared skills
#   With arg: sync only the named skill

set -e

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
SKILLS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/skills"
PLUGIN_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/plugin/skills"

# Skills that exist in both directories
shared_skills() {
  for d in "$SKILLS_DIR"/*/; do
    skill=$(basename "$d")
    if [ -d "$PLUGIN_DIR/$skill" ]; then
      echo "$skill"
    fi
  done
}

sync_skill() {
  local skill="$1"
  local src="$SKILLS_DIR/$skill"
  local dst="$PLUGIN_DIR/$skill"

  if [ ! -d "$src" ] || [ ! -d "$dst" ]; then
    echo "  SKIP $skill (not in both directories)"
    return
  fi

  # Sync non-SKILL.md files (references, scripts, assets) directly
  for subdir in references scripts assets; do
    if [ -d "$src/$subdir" ]; then
      mkdir -p "$dst/$subdir"
      cp -R "$src/$subdir/"* "$dst/$subdir/" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  done

  # For SKILL.md: preserve plugin frontmatter, sync body
  local src_md="$src/SKILL.md"
  local dst_md="$dst/SKILL.md"

  if [ ! -f "$src_md" ] || [ ! -f "$dst_md" ]; then
    echo "  SKIP $skill (missing SKILL.md)"
    return
  fi

  # Check if plugin has extra frontmatter keys (hooks, user-invocable, etc.)
  local has_plugin_keys=false
  if grep -q "^hooks:\|^user-invocable:\|^argument-hint:" "$dst_md" 2>/dev/null; then
    has_plugin_keys=true
  fi

  if [ "$has_plugin_keys" = true ]; then
    # Plugin has custom frontmatter — keep plugin copy as-is, warn if body diverges
    # Body comparison: strip frontmatter from both, diff the rest
    local src_body dst_body
    src_body=$(sed '1,/^---$/{ /^---$/!d; /^---$/{ x; /^---$/d; x; d; } }; /^---$/d' "$src_md" | tail -n +2)
    dst_body=$(sed '1,/^---$/{ /^---$/!d; /^---$/{ x; /^---$/d; x; d; } }; /^---$/d' "$dst_md" | tail -n +2)

    if [ "$src_body" != "$dst_body" ]; then
      echo "  DIVERGED $skill (plugin has custom frontmatter + different body — manual review needed)"
    else
      echo "  OK $skill (plugin frontmatter preserved, body matches)"
    fi
  else
    # No plugin-specific keys — safe to copy directly
    cp "$src_md" "$dst_md"
    echo "  SYNCED $skill"
  fi
}

echo "Syncing skills/ → plugin/skills/"
echo

if [ -n "$1" ]; then
  sync_skill "$1"
else
  for skill in $(shared_skills); do
    sync_skill "$skill"
  done
fi

echo
echo "Done."

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Pre-flight check hook — surfaces accumulated learning signals at session start.
# Outputs nothing if there are no signals (zero overhead for clean projects).

LEARNINGS_DIR=".learnings"
EVALS_DIR=".evals"
HANDOFF_DIR=".context-surfing"

# Count learning entries
if [ -f "$LEARNINGS_DIR/LEARNINGS.md" ]; then
  learning_count=$(grep -c '^\## \[LRN-' "$LEARNINGS_DIR/LEARNINGS.md" 2>/dev/null) || learning_count=0
else
  learning_count=0
fi

# Count error entries
if [ -f "$LEARNINGS_DIR/ERRORS.md" ]; then
  error_count=$(grep -c '^\## \[ERR-' "$LEARNINGS_DIR/ERRORS.md" 2>/dev/null) || error_count=0
else
  error_count=0
fi

# Count promotion-ready patterns
if [ -f "$LEARNINGS_DIR/LEARNINGS.md" ]; then
  promo_count=$(grep -c 'promotion_ready' "$LEARNINGS_DIR/LEARNINGS.md" 2>/dev/null) || promo_count=0
else
  promo_count=0
fi

# Count failed evals
if [ -f "$EVALS_DIR/EVAL_INDEX.md" ]; then
  eval_fail_count=$(grep -c '| fail |' "$EVALS_DIR/EVAL_INDEX.md" 2>/dev/null) || eval_fail_count=0
else
  eval_fail_count=0
fi

# Count handoff files
if [ -d "$HANDOFF_DIR" ]; then
  handoff_count=$(find "$HANDOFF_DIR" -name "handoff-*.md" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
else
  handoff_count=0
fi

# Calculate total signals
signals=$((learning_count + error_count + promo_count + eval_fail_count + handoff_count))

# Only output if there are signals
if [ "$signals" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "<pre-flight-check>"
  echo "Active learnings: $learning_count | Recent errors: $error_count | Promotion-ready: $promo_count | Failed evals: $eval_fail_count | Handoffs: $handoff_count"

  # Surface high-priority items
  if [ "$promo_count" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "Promotion-ready patterns exist — consider running /learning-aggregator."
  fi

  if [ "$eval_fail_count" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "Failed evals detected — consider running /eval-creator run before starting new work."
  fi

  if [ "$handoff_count" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "Unread handoff files from previous sessions — read before starting new work."
  fi

  echo "</pre-flight-check>"
fi

2. Extract promotion-ready patterns where `eval_candidate` is true.

3. Check cache-memory at `/tmp/gh-aw/cache-memory/eval-created-patterns.json` for patterns that already have eval cases. Skip duplicates.

9. Emit the creation results as structured YAML under key `eval_creator_ci` with `mode: create`.

10. Post a summary comment listing the new eval cases created.

11. Commit the new files with message: "chore: add eval cases from learning-aggregator-ci [skip ci]".

12. Do not modify source code files. Only write to `.evals/` directory.

# Skill Tester

Validates all interactive (non-CI) skills in this repo. Runs the Anthropic skill-creator's `quick_validate.py` plus project-specific checks.

## When to Use

- After adding or modifying a skill
- Before committing changes
- Before submitting the plugin for Anthropic review
- As part of the outer loop when eval-creator needs to verify skill quality

## Checks

### 1. Anthropic Spec Validation

Run `quick_validate.py` on every skill in `skills/` (excluding `-ci` variants):

```bash
for d in skills/*/; do
  skill=$(basename "$d")
  [[ "$skill" == *-ci ]] && continue
  python3 .claude/skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py "$d"
done
```

**Pass criteria:** Exit code 0 for every skill. Frontmatter has only allowed keys (`name`, `description`, `license`, `allowed-tools`, `metadata`, `compatibility`). Name is kebab-case, max 64 chars. Description max 1024 chars, no angle brackets.

### 2. Project Convention Checks

For each skill directory:

| Check | Rule | Severity |
|-------|------|----------|
| Name matches folder | Frontmatter `name` == directory name | Error |
| Line limit | SKILL.md under 500 lines (soft), under 600 lines (hard) | Warning / Error |
| No README.md | Skill folders must not contain README.md | Error |
| Scripts executable | All `.sh` files in `scripts/` must have execute permission | Error |
| References exist | Files referenced in SKILL.md body actually exist in `references/` | Warning |
| Description non-empty | Description field is present and non-empty | Error |

### 3. Cross-Reference Validation

Verify that all skills listed in these files actually exist as directories:

- `CLAUDE.md` — Skill References section
- `AGENTS.md` — Skill References section
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — Skill References section
- `README.md` — Skills table

Also verify reverse: every skill directory is listed in all four files.

### 4. Hook Script Testing

For each skill with a `scripts/` directory:

```bash
# Syntax check
bash -n scripts/*.sh

# Verify shebang
head -1 scripts/*.sh | grep -q "^#!/bin/bash"

# Verify executable
test -x scripts/*.sh
```

### 5. Plugin Skill Validation

For skills that exist in both `skills/` and `plugin/skills/`:

| Check | Rule |
|-------|------|
| Plugin frontmatter keys | Only Claude Code-specific keys (`hooks`, `user-invocable`, `argument-hint`) added beyond spec |
| Content alignment | Body content matches or plugin has extracted references |
| Beta markers consistent | If `skills/` copy has `[Beta]`, plugin copy should too |

## Output Format

```markdown
## Skill Test Results

**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Skills tested:** N
**Passed:** N
**Warnings:** N
**Failed:** N

### Failures
- [skill-name]: [check]: [error message]

### Warnings
- [skill-name]: [check]: [warning message]

### All Passed
- [list of clean skills]
```

## Running

Invoke manually:
```
/skill-tester
```

Or run the script directly:
```bash
bash skills/skill-tester/scripts/run-tests.sh
```

## What This Skill Does NOT Do

- Does not test CI skills (use `skill-tester-ci` for those)
- Does not modify skills — reports findings only
- Does not run behavioral evals (trigger testing) — use skill-creator's `run_eval.py` for that
- Does not replace the eval-creator regression framework — this tests skill structure, not promoted rules

# Hook Integration

Optional automatic triggering of self-healing on command failures and similar signals.

## Claude Code / Codex

### PostToolUse on Bash (recommended)

Detects non-zero exit codes and injects a system reminder pointing the agent at the heal loop.

`.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "./skills/self-healing/scripts/detect-failure.sh"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

Token overhead: ~80 tokens injected only on Bash failures. Silent on success.

### Combined with self-improvement

If you're also using self-improvement's `PostToolUse` hook, chain them. Both are read-only on the tool result — order doesn't matter, but put self-healing first so its trigger fires before the broader self-improvement reminder.

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [
        { "type": "command", "command": "./skills/self-healing/scripts/detect-failure.sh" },
        { "type": "command", "command": "./skills/self-improvement/scripts/error-detector.sh" }
      ]
    }]
  }
}
```

### Passing Active-Skill into new-heal.sh

When invoking the helper script from inside a skill flow, set `ACTIVE_SKILL` so it lands in the HEAL entry:

```bash
ACTIVE_SKILL=verify-gate ./skills/self-healing/scripts/new-heal.sh node_version_mismatch env_drift
```

The script reads `$ACTIVE_SKILL` from the environment and falls back to `none`.

## GitHub Copilot

Copilot doesn't support hooks. Add a self-healing prompt to `.github/copilot-instructions.md`:

```markdown
## Self-Healing

When a command, test, or build fails during a task, don't paper over it. Run the heal loop:

1. Diagnose the root cause from the error output
2. Search `.learnings/HEALS.md` for an existing fix (Pattern-Key match)
3. Apply or write the patch (artifacts go under `.learnings/heals/<HEAL-ID>/`)
4. Verify by re-running the failing operation; require success
5. File a `HEAL-YYYYMMDD-XXX` entry to `.learnings/HEALS.md` with status `verified`

Ask in chat: "Should I run the self-healing loop on this failure?"
```

## Troubleshooting

### "The detect-failure hook fires but the agent doesn't run the heal loop"

The hook is advisory — it injects a reminder, not a forced workflow. If the agent is ignoring it, check:

1. The skill is enabled in the active plugin set (`gh skill list`)
2. The skill's description triggers on the current task type (re-read the description)
3. There's no conflicting instruction in `CLAUDE.md` or active skills telling the agent to "just retry"

### "Every hook fires gives spurious heal prompts"

The hook only fires on non-zero exit. If you're getting too many prompts, it's because too many commands are failing — fix those and the noise drops. If a specific command legitimately exits non-zero (e.g. a `grep` that's expected to miss), wrap it: `grep ... || true`.

### "I want different triggers per project"

Override the hook script path per project. Each `.claude/settings.json` can point at a local copy of `detect-failure.sh` with project-specific logic.
